coverage: format-v2 seed — all five committed LiveEnvelope kinds, replace-to-delta `_id` continuity, auth/live apply-before-ack, equal-data-version authorization replacement, terminal delete, quarantine, and exact duplicate re-ACK, durable_bytes, connection-wide resync, wrapper framing, and first negatives; remaining malformed-offer, cancelled-drain, arm-mismatch, grant-loss, and virtual-time coverage is tracked by issues/20260725-0093-p1-fixture-corpus-coverage.md

fixtures.name: durable.live_replace.basic
fixtures.notes: Whole-result refresh; the wire default. Version guard admits 41 > 40.

fixtures.name: durable.live_delta.apply_by_id
fixtures.notes: Delta-vs-replace is the server's choice (D3 fact 4): a conformant client implements both and never infers query shape from which arrives.

fixtures.name: durable.live_delta.stale_version_dropped
fixtures.notes: Version guard: a frame at or below the held version is dropped without effect (LLP 0095 §1.3).

fixtures.name: durable.replace_then_delta.identity_continuity
fixtures.notes: Format-v2 multi-step witness: live_replace establishes `_id` todo_1, then live_delta id todo_1 updates that exact row. A corpus client keyed on user field `id` cannot pass.

fixtures.name: durable.current_as_of.adopts_token_without_rows
fixtures.notes: Known CurrentAsOf obligation: advance version and adopt the mandatory fresh token without replacing or mutating held rows (LLP 0091 §0B.2).

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without reapplying the snapshot

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_snapshot_apply_then_ack
fixtures.notes: Format-v2 level-triggered sequence: quarantine first, atomically apply the superseding snapshot, only then release the exact ackToken. A redelivery remains acknowledgeable and never re-applies equal-version rows.

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without reapplying the snapshot

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_authorization_snapshot_same_data_version
fixtures.notes: Authorization and data versions are orthogonal. A first-seen exact resolution at the authenticated new authorization epoch atomically replaces rows and becomes acknowledgeable even when its snapshot data version equals the held version; the ordinary live-frame strict-greater version guard does not apply. Only an exact redelivery may skip reapplication and re-acknowledge the same token.

expect.redelivery: re-acknowledge the same token without repeating the terminal delete

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_terminal_delete_apply_then_ack
fixtures.notes: A terminalDelete resolution carries no snapshot (wire omission and JSON null both decode as absent). The client first makes rows unreadable, atomically destroys the exact materialization and installs its terminal fence, and only then acknowledges the exact token. Exact redelivery re-acknowledges without repeating destruction.

fixtures.name: auth.live.invalidation_without_snapshot_quarantines
fixtures.notes: An obligation without a satisfying snapshot makes held rows unreadable and is not acknowledged. Level-triggered delivery continues until a resolution can be applied.

fixtures.name: auth.live.foreign_obligation_never_acknowledged
fixtures.notes: The full obligation scope names a subscription this client does not hold. It is surfaced and ignored, never acknowledged on behalf of a foreign live owner.

fixtures.name: durable.resync_required.subscription_scoped
fixtures.notes: Reason strings are an open set: recovery is identical for every reason, and an unknown reason must not change the transition.

fixtures.name: durable.resync_required.connection_wide_clear_retained
fixtures.notes: No subscription_id + clear_retained: the whole outbox is untrusted (overflow class). The frame crosses the lane boundary: retained ephemeral overlays blank too (LLP 0059 cross-lane rule).

equivalenceClass.permittedEquivalent: socket close/reconnect with fresh subscribe achieving the same transitions
equivalenceClass.reference: in-place synthesized connection-wide clear-retained resync sentinel (reason durable_bytes_undecodable, client-synthesized, never wire-emitted)

fixtures.name: socket.durable_bytes.forced_resync
fixtures.notes: D3 fact 2b: a KNOWN kind with a REQUIRED recovery action. The payload's outbox lease was released at socket handoff; ignoring this frame is non-conformant (silent permanent staleness).

fixtures.name: negative.unknown_kind.skipped
fixtures.notes: Unknown kinds are skip-not-crash defense-in-depth (new kinds are always offer-gated, so a conformant server never sends one ungated). Contrast socket.durable_bytes.forced_resync: KNOWN kind, required action.

fixtures.name: negative.unknown_field.tolerated
fixtures.notes: Unknown fields on known kinds are ignored, never fatal (the acceptance grammar wins over schema closure where they diverge — LLP 0093 D1).

fixtures.name: poll.wrapped_durable.unwrap
fixtures.notes: Lane-P framing: durable envelopes arrive wrapped ({"Durable":{"payload":[u8…]}}) over the HTTP drain and unwrapped over the socket. Wrapper handling is a lane obligation, not core.

fixtures.name: poll.acknowledged_batch.malformed_item_forces_resync
fixtures.notes: The poll-lane analogue of fact 2b (LLP 0095 §1.4 T-DB-P): after the ownership cut the malformed item is lost exactly like a durable_bytes payload, so it forces the same connection-wide resync class — and must never abort the remainder. Format v2 pins sub_fixture_1 in the population and subsumes the remainder item's actions AND transitions under deliver_batch_remainder.
